Maria (customer): Hi - we've got a bunch of users hitting 403 on the OAuth redirect step when signing in with GitHub and Google. They get sent back to our app with `error=access_denied` or sometimes the page says "state_mismatch". Happening to ~12 users in last hour, started after we rolled a config change.
Sam (support): Sorry you're hitting this Maria. Quick Qs: Are these users behind a corporate proxy / SSO? Any browser type patterns? Also, can you paste the exact redirect URL you registered in the GitHub/Google app?
Maria (customer): Most are Chrome on Mac, a couple Safari on iOS. We register https://app.company.com/auth/callback (no trailing slash). Some affected users have work accounts behind a proxy.
Sam (support): Thanks. Two common causes: 1) state param lost/changed by redirect chain (proxy stripping query) or 2) mismatch in the registered redirect URI (trailing slash / port / scheme). We'll escalate to eng to look at raw auth logs.
Sam (support): @dev-bot, can you pull the last 50 auth errors for org_id=423?
dev-bot: Retrieved 46 entries; sample log lines (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T14:05:22Z] auth: oauth_callback failure user_id=xxxx client=github org=423 err=state_mismatch received_state=abc123 expected_state=def456
[2026-03-15T14:06:01Z] auth: oauth_callback failure user_id=yyyy client=google org=423 err=invalid_scope
[2026-03-15T14:07:10Z] auth: oauth_callback failure user_id=zzzz client=github org=423 err=missing_state
```
Sam (support): Looks like we have both state_mismatch and missing_state. @Kevin can you take a look at the callback handler and any proxy / ingress rewrite rules for app.company.com?
Kevin (eng): On it. Early thought: our last deploy added an auth proxy (ingress) that rewrites URLs and sets a cookie for `code_verifier` to implement PKCE. If that proxy strips or reorders query params, `state` can be lost. Also if the proxy sets `SameSite` on the cookie incorrectly, the browser may not send it back.
Kevin (eng): Repro steps I'm going to run locally:
1) Start auth flow -> get redirected to provider with `state` and `code_challenge`
2) Provider redirects to https://app.company.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=...
3) Ingress should pass through query intact and our app should validate state and exchange code with `code_verifier` from cookie.
If query params are stripped or cookie not sent (SameSite=Lax for cross-site POSTs), we'll fail.
Owen (sre): I can tail the ingress logs for the actual raw request. Kevin, can you add a temporary log to dump the incoming querystring at the proxy level? We should also capture User-Agent to see if it's likely Safari (which has stricter cookie rules).
Maria (customer): We can reproduce with one of our test accounts. What should we try in the meantime to unblock users?
Sam (support): Short-term: ask affected users to use incognito or a different browser (to avoid extension/proxy interference) and confirm the redirect URI exactly matches what's in the OAuth app settings (including trailing slash and https).
Sam (support): Longer-term: engineering should: 1) ensure ingress forwards full query string, 2) move state validation to server-side storage tied to a short-lived session cookie (instead of only relying on client-side state param), or 3) persist PKCE `code_verifier` server-side keyed by a secure session cookie with SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly.
Kevin (eng): Quick diagnostics I ran: when I hit the callback behind the proxy with a simulated provider redirect, the proxy was normalizing the URL and dropping empty query params — but not `state`. However, I found a different bug: our cookie path for `code_verifier` was `/v1` while the callback is `/auth`, so cookie wasn't sent. That would show up as missing `code_verifier` and sometimes we return state_mismatch because we clear server-side session when verifier missing.
Kevin (eng): Patch plan: 1) change cookie path to `/` for PKCE cookie, 2) ensure cookie flags: `SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly`, 3) add more robust logging for `state` vs expected, 4) add a fallback check to allow code exchange if server-side session has the pending flow. I'll open a PR.
Owen (sre): Also double-check our OAuth app settings on provider dashboard: redirect URIs must match exactly. If we have a vanity host or CDN in front, ensure that host is the one registered. GitHub treats trailing slash and query params differently.
Maria (customer): Appreciate the rapid response — do you need any of our logs? We can share a failing redirect URL and an example `Set-Cookie` header from browser devtools.
Sam (support): Yes please share: 1) the full redirect URL you saw in the browser address bar after provider redirect, 2) a screenshot of network tab showing request to `/auth/callback`, 3) value of `Set-Cookie` for our site prior to redirect (we just need header string). You can DM them to me.
Kevin (eng): Opening a PR with the cookie path fix and added ingress passthrough tests. ETA for deploy: ~2 hours assuming tests pass. If that doesn't fix, next step is to add server-side state persistence.
Maria (customer): Great — we'll hold off contacting customers until you confirm. Thanks.
Sam (support): Marking this thread for follow-up. I'll update once deploy is live. :thumbsup:
(dev-bot): PR #5123 opened by kevin: 'pkce: set cookie path=/ and SameSite=None on auth cookie'
Sam (support): Deployed the patch to staging, rolling to prod now. Will monitor auth-errors metric and the specific org 423.
Owen (sre): Monitoring shows auth_error.rate for org 423 decreasing after rollout. Current tail: 2 in last 15m vs 18 before.
Maria (customer): Confirmed with our test account — login now completes. Thanks everyone!
Sam (support): Excellent. I'll close the ticket once we see sustained reduction. If anything else crops up, please reopen.
